unit_index.unit_title: Completed zeta turns RH into reality of all xi zeros
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The bridge is the completed function ξ together with s=1/2+it: multiplication changes the analytic object while retaining the nontrivial-zero question, and the affine change sends the critical line to the real t-axis.
unit_index.interpretation: Completion packages analytic continuation, the pole, gamma symmetry, and the reflection s↦1−s into one entire even object. Recentring at the fixed line of the reflection turns a two-dimensional zero-location problem into a real-rootedness problem.

unit_index.source_title: Problems of the Millennium: The Riemann Hypothesis
unit_index.unit_title: Euler product, Mellin inversion, and residues make zeros govern primes
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The Euler product, the logarithm, the weighted counting function, Mellin-type integration, Fourier inversion, and residue calculus form the bridge from primes to zeros. The transform preserves enough counting information to be inverted while exposing analytic singularities.
unit_index.interpretation: Each representation relocates the difficulty. Multiplicative prime data become additive after taking logarithms; the transform makes analytic continuation and inversion available; residues compress global oscillation into discrete singularity data.

unit_index.source_title: Problems of the Millennium: The Riemann Hypothesis
unit_index.unit_title: Zeta is a prototype, and solving it may require the general L-function problem
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Modular parametrization bridges elliptic curves to functional equations, while simultaneous Laplacian and Hecke eigenfunctions bridge Maass waveforms to Euler products. These bridges preserve arithmetic structure but relocate the burden to modularity or spectral theory.
unit_index.interpretation: Generalization is not only enlargement of scope; it can expose the missing invariant. The analytic package shared by L-functions may be easier to understand through its sources—geometry, automorphy, Hecke action—even though proving membership in that package is itself difficult.

unit_index.source_title: Problems of the Millennium: The Riemann Hypothesis

unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The argument principle turns a two-dimensional zero set into an integer contour invariant, and ξ turns critical-line zeros into real sign changes. Exact integer rounding bridges numerical evaluation to a certified count only when the numerical error is controlled.
unit_index.interpretation: This is certificate composition: one method supplies exhaustive cardinality and another supplies witnesses with the desired property. Their agreement upgrades numerical detection to a finite-range proof.

unit_index.source_title: Problems of the Millennium: The Riemann Hypothesis
unit_index.unit_title: RH becomes negativity of an explicit-formula quadratic form
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Abstracts only the source-visible common proof obligation—a sign condition—and compares an asserted classical uniform-negativity criterion with a geometrically forced finite-field sign, while auditing which part of the classical representation is absent.
unit_index.interpretation: Within the visible boundary, RH is recast as a uniform negativity requirement over a restricted family built from g, rather than as separate assertions about individual zeros. The finite-field case supplies a comparison mechanism: an algebraic index theorem forces negative semidefiniteness of the self-intersection form on degree-zero divisors. This gains a structural sign target and shows how geometry can force the analogous sign, but it does not identify the missing classical right-hand side or establish a transfer from divisor intersections to the classical problem. The remaining burden is to recover the omitted quadratic expression from a wider span and prove its negativity for every admissible function, with the two vanishing-integral constraints, the function class W, and the sign convention intact.

unit_index.interpretation: The analogy is useful when it predicts structural obligations rather than merely matching distributions. unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Extracts the certification design by separating completeness closure, correction of approximate counts, and overlapping reproducibility checks without inflating their independence.
unit_index.interpretation: Source fact: the computation extends beyond the target Gram point through five Rosser-valid blocks, then invokes a cited counting theorem to certify that the first 1,500,000,001 zeros are simple and on the critical line in the stated rectangle. A range whose earlier argument shifts made Gram-block and interval counts approximate was rerun without shifts. Additional checks used the vectorized program on another machine and compared selected earlier ranges. Interpretation: finite certification combines endpoint closure with targeted reruns of known bookkeeping vulnerabilities and cross-machine or prior-range overlap. Boundary: these are checks of related program versions and hardware, not demonstrated independently developed implementations, and the conclusion is finite-height only.

unit_index.source_title: On the Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function in the Critical Strip. IV
unit_index.unit_title: Method-specific dominant errors yield conservative sign certification for Z at Gram points
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Separates analytic truncation, interpolation, and arithmetic errors, then explains why a margin converts their combined envelope into a sign certificate.
unit_index.interpretation: Source fact: the authors extend a prior rigorous error analysis to the larger height range and account for the CYBER 205's truncated 47- and 94-bit arithmetic. Interpolation dominates the error of method A, while truncation of the two-term Riemann-Siegel expansion dominates method B; other hardware terms are smaller. The fixed bounds actually used are deliberately larger than the derived safe bounds, and method B determines every needed Gram-point sign. Interpretation: an approximation plus an absolute-error envelope is the interface from floating-point output to a certified exact sign. Boundary: the detailed derivation is referred to earlier work, and the stated bounds apply to these methods, machines, and range.

unit_index.source_title: On the Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function in the Critical Strip. IV
unit_index.unit_title: Gram-block types drift toward length-dependent symmetric-looking distributions
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Reorganizes the data by conditioning variable and separates stable-looking within-length shape from across-height drift and sampling uncertainty.
unit_index.interpretation: Source fact: exact finite counts over 1.5 billion Gram intervals show a slowly decreasing fraction of length-one blocks, increasing longer blocks, and, for several fixed lengths, type frequencies that appear to approach length-dependent distributions with missing zeros favoring outer intervals. The authors explicitly withhold a limiting claim for sparsely sampled lengths at least seven. Interpretation: conditioning on block length exposes a pattern hidden by aggregate occupancy, while changes across height reveal finite-range drift rather than a frozen law. Approximate reflection of paired type frequencies is empirical, not a symmetry theorem. Boundary: the tables do not identify or prove convergence to any probability distribution.

unit_index.source_title: On the Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function in the Critical Strip. IV
unit_index.unit_title: Zero-count identities and adjacent-block searches audit exceptions to Rosser's rule
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Connects an invariant and an adversarial pattern to distinguish correctness checks from search completeness.
unit_index.interpretation: Source fact: a counting identity relating the numbers of Gram intervals with j zeros supplies an internal consistency check. The run classifies 3,055 Rosser exceptions; every observed missing pair lies in the preceding or succeeding block. The source then gives an unobserved 0,0,1,3-type configuration for which searching only the nearest adjacent block would fail. Interpretation: the count identity audits conservation of zeros, while the hypothetical pattern is a counterfactual completeness test for an empirically successful recovery heuristic. Boundary: adjacent-block recovery worked on all observed exceptions but is not logically complete, and the source does not specify a complete replacement algorithm.

unit_index.source_title: On the Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function in the Critical Strip. IV
unit_index.unit_title: Rosser exceptions, S extremes, a closest pair, and large Gram-point values probe finite tails
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Places heterogeneous rare-event measurements on comparable local scales and explicitly audits the reach of correlations seen in the finite sample.
unit_index.interpretation: Source fact: the finite run records Rosser-exception types and local extremes of S, a closest observed zero pair with normalized separation about 0.00034, and the largest sampled positive and negative Gram-point Z values. The latter occur between neighboring zeros separated by about 3.85 and 3.65 local Gram intervals. Interpretation: normalizing gaps permits comparison across height, while S, block pattern, gap, and amplitude provide multiple observables of rare local configurations. Their co-occurrence generates hypotheses but does not supply a causal mechanism or asymptotic frequency. Boundary: these are records from one finite computation, not evidence of tail independence or a limiting law.

unit_index.source_title: On the Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function in the Critical Strip. IV
unit_index.unit_title: Finite Gram statistics suggest but do not explain an unknown probabilistic law
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Separates explanatory model-building from finite certification and identifies the exact observable a future theory must reproduce.
unit_index.interpretation: Source fact: the authors say the observed Gram-block type frequencies for lengths three through six appear to tend to length-dependent discrete convex distributions and ask for a probabilistic model that could explain them. They separately note that results depending on a finite verified-height parameter may improve after the larger computation, but do not trace those consequences. Interpretation: the computation ends by identifying a compression problem: replace many empirical type counts by a testable probability law. That missing model is distinct from enlarging a finite RH verification range. Boundary: no limiting distribution, downstream bound, or global evidence for RH is established here.

unit_index.source_title: A new lower bound for the de Bruijn-Newman constant
unit_index.unit_title: A nonreal Jensen zero certifies a lower bound for the de Bruijn-Newman constant
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Identifies a change in proof burden—from global real-rootedness to a finite existential obstruction—and states what a negative search cannot establish.
unit_index.interpretation: Source-grounded mathematics: the note defines a threshold Λ separating parameters for which H_λ has only real zeros from those with nonreal zeros, records that RH would imply Λ≤0, and cites [2] for the implication that a nonreal zero of a Jensen polynomial G_m(·;λ) gives λ<Λ. Conceptual interpretation: passing from H_λ through its moments to a finite Jensen polynomial changes a global real-rootedness question into an existential obstruction search: one valid nonreal root suffices, whereas failure to find one proves nothing. The remaining burden is reliable nonreal-root certification, not merely numerical approximation. Uncertainty: the defining integral and exact Jensen normalization are OCR-damaged, and the criterion is cited rather than derived in this span.

unit_index.source_title: A new lower bound for the de Bruijn-Newman constant
unit_index.unit_title: Count all real roots instead of approximating every polynomial zero
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Separates an exact algebraic decision procedure from its floating-point realization and exposes interval completeness and sign correctness as independent proof obligations.
unit_index.interpretation: Source-grounded mathematics: for an exact polynomial with the stated simple-root condition, a Sturm chain turns endpoint sign-variation differences into the number of real roots on [a,b]. The reported algorithm applies this to successive Jensen polynomials and uses Newton continuation only to approximate a complex root as a check. Conceptual interpretation: the computation is reframed from locating every root to deciding whether all roots are real. A root-count deficit supports the desired conclusion only when the interval contains every real root and the numerically evaluated Sturm signs are validated; floating-point sign computation is a separate obligation from the exact Sturm theorem. Uncertainty: interval and precision details continue in later units, and minor OCR substitutions affect polynomial notation.

unit_index.source_title: A new lower bound for the de Bruijn-Newman constant
unit_index.unit_title: Witness degree and required precision explode as lambda approaches zero
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Extracts an algorithm-specific difficulty indicator while sharply limiting what a finite computational table licenses.
unit_index.interpretation: Source-grounded mathematics: the finite table reports minimal obstructing Jensen degrees rising from 16 at λ=-50 to 41 at -20, 97 at -10, and 406 at -5; each listed polynomial has degree minus two real roots, the -5 run used 250-digit working precision, and the displayed conjugate pair moves closer to the real axis as λ increases. Conceptual interpretation: this is a sharp finite-sample escalation for this particular obstruction-search algorithm—higher-degree polynomials and less-separated nonreal roots accompany the approach toward zero. The Sturm count supplies the reported nonreal-root conclusion; the tabulated complex pair is an additional approximation. The data support Λ>-5 and a practical warning, not a phase transition, asymptotic degree law, universal hardness claim, or certified error bound equal to the working precision.

unit_index.source_title: A new lower bound for the de Bruijn-Newman constant
unit_index.unit_title: Bound tails first, then exploit exponential trapezoidal convergence
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Decomposes numerical reliability into separate error channels and explains why even analyticity changes the appropriate quadrature representation.
unit_index.interpretation: Source-grounded mathematics: each moment is split at a cutoff whose discarded tail is analytically bounded; the positive series for Φ is truncated against a precision-dependent remainder target; and the finite integral is evaluated by composite trapezoidal rules after Romberg extrapolation was observed to degrade accuracy. The cited theorem explains exponential trapezoidal convergence for the even analytic integrand, while mesh halving supplied an empirical digit-stability check. Conceptual interpretation: the pipeline assigns distinct controls to tail truncation, kernel-series truncation, and discretization, and chooses quadrature to match analytic structure rather than merely increasing precision. These local controls do not by themselves certify rounding-error propagation through Jensen coefficients and Sturm signs.

unit_index.source_title: A new lower bound for the de Bruijn-Newman constant
unit_index.unit_title: Sturm sign stability and a global root interval complete the certificate
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Separates geometric completeness from arithmetic reliability and identifies the expected count pattern as a diagnostic rather than proof by itself.
unit_index.interpretation: Source-grounded mathematics: the paper generates the Sturm sequence coefficientwise, counts on [a,0] because real roots are known to be negative, enlarges the interval when an apparent deficit is not accompanied by a located complex root, and reports that [-5000,0] sufficed at λ=-5. Abrupt anomalous count drops disappeared when precision was raised, restoring the degree or degree-minus-two pattern; an explicitly computed complex root remained an extra check. Conceptual interpretation: interval coverage and numerical sign stability diagnose two distinct failure modes—a real root outside the window and incorrect floating-point signs. Together they form the paper's reported checking strategy, but restored expected counts are not an independent exact-arithmetic certificate.

unit_index.unit_title: Short-interval lower means divide sharply according to whether an Euler product is available
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Fractional-power branches and Q(σ) connect analytic continuation to short-interval means; the Euler product later connects those means to coefficient mass.
unit_index.interpretation: The presence of an Euler product changes the available invariant from generic coefficients to controlled local prime factors. The paper treats that representation choice as a real method boundary, not a formatting difference.

unit_index.source_title: Some remarks on the mean value of the Riemann zeta-function and other Dirichlet series 1
unit_index.unit_title: Local Euler-factor mass forces a large mean on some line near one
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Separates the theorem's existential-over-lines content from a stronger fixed-line claim and reclassifies the local-mass story as a possible explanation rather than source-established mechanism; this exposes both the flexibility gained by maximizing and the localization information forfeited.
unit_index.interpretation: Source fact: under one of two stated Euler-product conditions, Theorem 1 gives a qualitative lower bound for the maximum of Q(σ) over a narrow range of lines to the right of one, and the span then begins a proof by contradiction. The quantifier over σ is important: the theorem guarantees a large value somewhere in that range, not on a prescribed line. As a labeled inference only, this freedom may let later Euler-product information become visible without first locating its effective line; that mechanism is not proved in this unit. The representation gains an existential lower-bound target but loses fixed-line control, and the contradiction still must be discharged by the subsequent lemmas.

unit_index.source_title: Some remarks on the mean value of the Riemann zeta-function and other Dirichlet series 1
unit_index.unit_title: Assuming the lower bound fails supplies global mean control and a subharmonic pointwise ceiling
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Decomposes the mean-to-supremum bridge into zero removal, boundary averaging, area averaging, and an interior-radius constraint. This replaces the unsupported compactness analogy with the actual analytic conversion and identifies its loss of boundary coverage.
unit_index.interpretation: The negation of Theorem 1 supplies the integral control recorded in Lemma 1, while Lemma 2 turns averaged control into a pointwise interior ceiling. Its concrete mechanism is local: form an auxiliary product over the zeros inside a disk so that its boundary modulus agrees with |F|, use the center-versus-boundary logarithmic inequality, pass to a disk-area average, and then apply the integral mean inequality to |F|^{2k}. This gains pointwise control from an average but only after choosing a disk that stays away from the t-interval edges; it does not itself contradict the assumed failure. Zero counting and contour use are downstream context, not results of this span.

unit_index.source_title: Some remarks on the mean value of the Riemann zeta-function and other Dirichlet series 1
unit_index.unit_title: Zero density carves the t-interval into long regions where a logarithmic branch is controllable
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Factors the construction by function: reciprocal-polynomial truncation detects zeros, density bounds limit contaminated blocks, and block excision converts that count into a restricted analytic domain. This also makes explicit the tradeoff between a coherent good set and the loss of uniform coverage.
unit_index.interpretation: The proof converts zero control into a usable domain in three stages: Jensen's inequality bounds zeros in unit-height disks; the truncated Dirichlet series M_H for F^{-1} enters through F(s)M_H(s)-1 as a zero detector yielding a density estimate; then logarithmic t-blocks containing zeros, together with neighboring margins, are deleted to form the retained set I_3. The key conceptual operation is therefore not a topological removal but a quantitative pipeline from an analytic detector to a count and then to a geometric restriction of the integration domain. It gains zero-free regions on which the subsequent coefficient asymptotic is posed, while losing bad blocks and edge regions and giving no everywhere-in-t conclusion.

unit_index.interpretation: The proof composes two independent resources: multiplicativity supplies mass, while discrete calculus forces some derivative to register variation of that mass across nearby lines.

unit_index.unit_title: Rewrite the classical functional equation in exponential product form before fractionalizing
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Reorients one reflection identity in both directions and extracts its comparison role: any proposed extension should recover the displayed coupling at integer order. The representation gains a concrete calibration constraint, while the construction of noninteger coefficients or operators and any computational simplification remain separate proof burdens.
unit_index.interpretation: Equations (3.1) and (3.2) are best used as an integer-order reflection template: a kth derivative of zeta on one side of s↔1-s is related to a finite h,n-indexed combination of gamma and zeta derivatives on the other, weighted by formula-specific constants and trigonometric factors. Substituting s→1-s reverses the orientation of that same template. This gives a consistency target for a later noninteger analogue, but this span itself supplies neither a fractional identity nor a reduction of infinite sums.

unit_index.source_title: The Riemann hypothesis is true up to 3·10^12
unit_index.unit_title: Count-only certification saves storage and precision without weakening completeness
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: It identifies which witness detail the implementation discards for its count-oriented objective while explicitly separating that optimization from an absent global completeness proof.
unit_index.interpretation: The implementation changes its retained object from a high-precision zero database to the minimum local information needed for counting: after detecting a sign change, it does not zoom in with Shannon–Whittaker–Nyquist machinery or store a refined zero. Arb also reduces memory relative to MPFI, and the default lattice empirically isolates nearly all zeros directly. This span supports the efficiency tradeoff only; it does not contain the surrounding global completeness argument, so sign changes alone must not be described here as a complete certificate.

unit_index.source_title: The Riemann hypothesis is true up to 3·10^12
unit_index.unit_title: The cost of rigor is separated from algorithmic and hardware throughput
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: It audits a performance comparison by decomposing the normalized number into algorithmic, hardware, sampling, and epistemic components it does not normalize away.
unit_index.interpretation: The reported metric is processed length of the critical half-line per GHz-hour, not zeros per hour. Even that normalization leaves major task differences: FFT acceleration versus direct Riemann–Siegel evaluation, samples per zero, multiprecision rigorous arithmetic versus hardware floating point, bound and parameter tuning, and modest hyper-threading gains. Throughput is therefore not a single invariant of an algorithm; precision, sampling, and rigor define materially different computations.

unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: It separates a finite computational premise from the analytic transfer theorem and calculates the exact epistemic reach of their composition.
unit_index.interpretation: A finite verified-height result becomes an unconditional global bound only through a previously proved threshold theorem for the de Bruijn–Newman heat-flow family. The source defines Lambda, distinguishes RH's equivalent upper sign Lambda<=0 from the proved lower sign Lambda>=0, and inserts the achieved height into a published threshold to obtain Lambda<=0.2. The next threshold is not reached, so neither Lambda<0.19 nor RH is licensed.

unit_index.source_title: The Riemann-Siegel Formula and Large Scale Computations of the Riemann Zeta Function
unit_index.unit_title: Why Riemann-Siegel changes feasible verification
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The Riemann-Siegel representation replaces a long general summation method by a specialized critical-line formula. Extended precision trades throughput for a wider trustworthy numerical domain.
unit_index.interpretation: Algorithmic compression makes large searches possible, but epistemic certification requires tracking both analytic and machine error. Fast evaluation supplies local evidence; it is not itself a proof that every zero in a range was found.

unit_index.source_title: The Riemann-Siegel Formula and Large Scale Computations of the Riemann Zeta Function
unit_index.unit_title: Riemann-Siegel main sum plus asymptotic remainder
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The real Z representation, saddle parameter p, correction functions C_j, and Stirling phase connect analytic contour structure to an implementable cosine sum.
unit_index.interpretation: Choosing N at the saddle scale compresses critical-line evaluation to order sqrt(t). The remainder representation exposes a controllable accuracy ladder rather than one opaque approximation error.

unit_index.source_title: The Riemann-Siegel Formula and Large Scale Computations of the Riemann Zeta Function
unit_index.unit_title: Factor dominant saddle behavior, rescale, truncate, and extend the path
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The sequence exposes which structure is exact and which is approximate: factorization and recentering isolate local correction data, series truncation reduces that data to finitely many terms, and path extension changes their evaluation into reusable coefficient integrals. The gain is a computable correction sum; the remaining burdens are the truncation analysis and the unquantified path-extension error in this span.
unit_index.interpretation: The remainder is reorganized by factoring the dominant terms near a=i sqrt(2 pi t), introducing the rapidly convergent residual g(x-a), then recentering exactly with x=u+2 pi i N and p=sqrt(t/(2 pi))-N. Truncating the g-series at K is the source-identified dominant approximation; extending Gamma_1 to Gamma is a later approximation that enables termwise integration and the finite sum of b_n c_n, but this span supplies no separate bound for that extension.

unit_index.source_title: The Riemann-Siegel Formula and Large Scale Computations of the Riemann Zeta Function
unit_index.unit_title: Argument-principle root count exposes the endpoint-obstruction
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Xi'/xi converts zeros into residues; symmetry compresses the contour to theta plus the argument term S(T). S is the bridge from exact global count to an averaged bound.
unit_index.interpretation: Local sign detection and global zero counting are different representations of the verification problem. The argument principle counts all zeros, including off-line ones, but pointwise contour control is too fragile for repeated computation.

unit_index.source_title: The Riemann-Siegel Formula and Large Scale Computations of the Riemann Zeta Function
unit_index.unit_title: Taylor-polynomial remainder coefficients trade symbolic preprocessing for fast evaluation
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The derivative scaling is the concrete representation bridge from formulas involving Psi derivatives to reusable polynomial tables. This trades one-time symbolic differentiation and coefficient generation for repeated polynomial evaluation, but it does not by itself certify runtime error or numerical conditioning.
unit_index.interpretation: The implementation changes variables by p=(z+1)/2, writes Psi(p)=Phi(z), and uses the exact scaling Psi^(n)(p)=2^n Phi^(n)(z) to convert the analytic correction functions C_0 through C_4 into Taylor polynomials in z. Maple generates thirty-digit coefficients offline, and each stored list is cut off once coefficient magnitude falls below 10^-20; the span does not show that centering improves conditioning or that this cutoff gives a uniform remainder bound.

unit_index.source_title: The Riemann-Siegel Formula and Large Scale Computations of the Riemann Zeta Function
unit_index.unit_title: Batch acceleration does not automatically accelerate a single Z evaluation
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The complex Dirichlet-sum form separates an easy phase factor from the labor-intensive partial sum, suggesting where an alternative approximation must act.
unit_index.interpretation: Throughput and latency are distinct complexity objectives. An approximation calibrated to the existing analytic error budget could be useful even if it does not recover the main sum to arbitrary precision.

unit_index.source_title: The De Bruijn-Newman constant is non-negative
unit_index.unit_title: Off-axis H_t asymptotics replace the missing t<0 Dirichlet series
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Identifies representation availability as the reason the proof moves off axis, without calling the evaluation curve an already chosen contour or importing later counting losses.
unit_index.interpretation: For Λ<t≤0 the lemma controls H_t and its logarithmic derivative at imaginary depth comparable to log x, with sharper information only when the depth coefficient is sufficiently large. The source contrasts usable t=0 Dirichlet-series access closer to the axis with negative-time expansions that converge rapidly only at logarithmic depth; it also distinguishes estimates that could hold on -C<t from the stronger Λ<t assumption required by the stated application.

unit_index.source_title: The De Bruijn-Newman constant is non-negative
unit_index.unit_title: First-term dominance converts saddle asymptotics into H_t and log-derivative control
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Combines dominant-term compression with a second representation change—from real-part/modulus information to derivative information via holomorphy—and states why nonvanishing is essential.
unit_index.interpretation: After saddle evaluation, the series for H_t is dominated by Q_{t,1}: moderate indices are quantitatively smaller relative to it, while negative saddle displacement makes the large-index tail summable. The resulting nonvanishing holomorphic ratio H_t/H_0 yields modulus control, and Borel–Carathéodory plus Cauchy estimates upgrade that control to a logarithmic-derivative bound.

unit_index.source_title: The De Bruijn-Newman constant is non-negative
unit_index.unit_title: Inverse-distance zero motion relaxes spacing fluctuations toward a local lattice

unit_index.interpretation: Backward heat evolution induces a principal-value inverse-distance ODE for the real zeros. The source-authored heuristic views local arithmetic progressions as equilibria and estimates how spacing fluctuations might relax over the available time; it then introduces a logarithmic Hamiltonian and inverse-square energy only formally, since the infinite sums are not absolutely convergent.

unit_index.interpretation: For each interval I, Q_I records time-integrated internal inverse-square energy. Comparing crude bounds across nested intervals locates a cutoff K whose slight enlargement K' adds only a small fraction of energy; integrating the finite Hamiltonian identity, bounding the far exterior, and absorbing the annular contribution then yields a polynomial integrated-energy bound.

unit_index.interpretation: Moderate/negligible weighted-sum bounds first make the infinite calculation integrable. Proposition 22 then proves absolute continuity, justifies interchanging the pair sum with time integration, differentiates the nearby weighted Hamiltonian, and decomposes the result into near/far terms; symmetrization, weight smoothness, replacement by classical-location interactions, and reference-interaction cancellation leave -4 times renormalized energy up to scale-relative negligible error.

unit_index.interpretation: Small time-zero renormalized energy bounds the sum of V over consecutive normalized gaps. Nonnegativity plus Markov's inequality forces a 1-o(1) fraction of these ratios toward one, but the cited theorem of Conrey and collaborators supplies a positive proportion of gaps below a fixed fraction of mean spacing under the relevant hypothesis, contradicting the assumed negative Λ.
